operator_io_quirks: Mixed quoting in DDL: pilot/aircraft use backticks, match/airport/airport_aircraft use double quotes; identifiers must be re-quoted with " and " doubled.
Table name `match` is a SQL keyword; must always be double-quoted in generated SQL and in pragma/sqlite_master lookups.
Column `%_Change_2007` starts with `%`; needs quoting and will exercise sqlparse tokenization (percent is not a normal identifier char).
Column `Date` is declared TEXT and stores non-ISO strings like 'March 26–27' (en-dash, no year); declared type dispatches to String fuzzer, not Date.
match.Winning_Pilot / match.Winning_Aircraft are declared TEXT but store integer-looking strings ('1','4','6'); FK to int PKs — storage class contradicts declared type.

aircraft.Max_Gross_Weight / Total_disk_area / Max_disk_Loading are varchar(50) holding formatted measurements with commas, units, superscript ² — String fuzzer will produce garbage, not these formats.
airport_aircraft has composite PK (Airport_ID, Aircraft_ID) and a separate non-PK `ID` column; composite-PK members get max_l0=30 in TS.
match.Round is REAL PK with values 1.0..7.0 (integer-valued floats); Number fuzzer with scale from `real` (no args) will perturb by ±0.01/±0.02.
All tables tiny (4–12 rows); original_values sampling (k=min(5,len)) will nearly exhaust the distinct values, so TS will mostly reuse originals.
No NOT NULL on match/airport/airport_aircraft columns despite PKs; sqlite allows NULL in non-INTEGER PKs, so TS may insert NULL PKs that survive.
airport_aircraft.ID is not a PK and not unique; TS will not dedupe it, so duplicates expected.
FKs all resolve to existing parents (pilot, aircraft, airport); no dangling FKs, no self-references, no cycles.
operator_ts_expectations: pilot.Pilot_Id, aircraft.Aircraft_ID, airport.Airport_ID: Number fuzzer, int scale 0 → range [-1,1] perturbed; PK dedupe keeps ~1–2 rows, so parent tables shrink drastically and FK children get few distinct values.
match.Round: Number(scale=4) from `real` → range [-10^4,10^4] floats; PK dedupe on floats almost never collides, so match keeps its full size.
match.Winning_Pilot / Winning_Aircraft: String fuzzer (declared TEXT) → random a-zA-Z0-9() strings, NOT integers; FK fill overrides with parent values only when parent non-empty, else NULL.
aircraft.Max_Gross_Weight etc.: String fuzzer with length range from varchar(50) → random 0–50 char strings; loses the '1,370 lb (635 kg)' format entirely.
airport.%_Change_2007: String fuzzer; '%' in elements triggers the replace('%','') variant, so '1.5%' becomes '1.5' in the pool — format lost.
match.Date: String fuzzer (TEXT) → random strings, not dates; any query filtering on date format will get implausible values (FN driver).
airport numeric columns (Total_Passengers etc.): Number(scale=4) → range [-10^4,10^4], far below real magnitudes (10^7–10^8); implausible values drive FN on range/aggregate queries.
airport_aircraft composite PK: both members get max_l0=30, so fresh draws capped; FK fill from airport/aircraft (which shrank) yields few distinct pairs → PK dedupe keeps few rows.
airport_aircraft.ID: Number fuzzer, no dedupe → duplicates; queries counting distinct ID will see ties (FP driver).
Small originals (≤12 rows) mean TS's 5-sample original_values nearly covers the table; with p=0.2 most draws reuse originals, so many units look like the original (weak discrimination).
pilot.Name: String fuzzer over 'a-zA-Z 0-9()' → random names, not 'Prof. Zackery Collins' style; LIKE/pattern queries on names get implausible values (FN).
No CHECK constraints and no NOT NULL on most columns → TS inserts NULLs freely; queries with IS NOT NULL / comparisons get NULL-heavy results (FP/FN mix).
